item.title: US envoys meet Zelensky in Dublin after talks with Putin in Moscow
item.description:
U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner met with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow Thursday to discuss Ukraine, after two days of U.S.-led talks between Russian and Ukrainian delegations in Abu Dhabi yielded no major breakthroughs. “I think progress was made. I think it was made earlier today,” Witkoff told reporters after the meeting at the Senate Palace of the Kremlin. “People didn't think that we were going to restart trilateral. We’ve restarted it. We’ve set a new meeting. This is what President [Donald] Trump wants to see." He went on to say that a European representative would be present for the next stage of the talks, which are set to look at the continent’s wider security arrangements. “They’re our partners, and it’s important for them to be involved,” he said. item.title: New York building collapse kills 8, including 2 children
item.description:
Six adults and two children were killed Wednesday afternoon when a three-story building at 1321 Flatbush Avenue collapsed into a construction site next door. Eighteen other people were injured in the collapse or responding to it. One of them remains in critical condition, Mayor Zohran Mamdani reported at a press conference Thursday afternoon. Many of the people impacted by the collapse are immigrants, the mayor said, including from Trinidad, Colombia and Mexico. One victim was a 26-year-old father from Ecuador, Today reported . José Luis Caguana Cosquillo leaves behind his pregnant wife and their first child. Two of the people killed were construction workers working on the excavation next door at the time of the collapse, City officials said. item.title: It Takes More Than 1 Activist To Kill a Data Center
item.description:
Social media is currently abuzz about Taylor Frazier McCollum, a Maryland woman who has become the face of the protest movement against a proposed data center on the site of a long-dead mall in Landover, Maryland, near Washington, D.C. In 2024, Prince George's County gave final planning approval to the $5 billion Brightseat Tech Park project, which would have created a massive hyperscale data center on the site of the old mall. Upon hearing that the project would be built roughly a mile from her home, Frazier McCollum, an unemployed single mother, began agitating against it. In June 2025, she launched a Change.org petition opposing the data center. That September, Prince George's County executive Aisha Braveboy issued a temporary moratorium on processing hyperscale data center permits, stalling the Landover project. item.title: HOA boards often make decisions behind closed doors. California should require they meet in public
item.description:
Guest Commentary written by William Fulton William Fulton is a professor of practice at UC San Diego and a condo owner. He is a former mayor of Ventura. Like millions of other Californians, I live in a community governed by a homeowners association. In my case the HOA operates a tall condo building in downtown San Diego. My wife and I pay a lot every month in assessments, and we get a lot in return: 24-hour concierge service, beautiful common areas, two full-time engineers who keep the building running, janitorial service and more. But we don’t really know what our HOA board does. We don’t know how they build our budget, why they enter into contracts or how they make many other decisions that affect our financial investment in our building. Our board meets almost exclusively in closed session, communicates with us mostly via email, delivers a budget to us with an increased assessment…

item.description:
